sources.title: USSR Law No. 1360-I, 14 March 1990: creation of the Presidency and constitutional amendments
sources.publisher: USSR Congress of People's Deputies; original law held by GARF, reproduced by Bavarian State Library, 1000 Schluesseldokumente
sources.access_method: Russian original-law transcription read; four GARF facsimile leaves visually inspected

claims.text: The law creates the USSR Presidency; new Article 127 identifies the President as head of the Soviet state.
claims.locator: Section I; Section II.3, Article 127; facsimile pages 1 and 3

claims.text: The law removes the preamble's leading-party sentence and replaces Article 6 with participation by the CPSU, other parties, organizations and movements.
claims.locator: Section II.1-2, Article 6; facsimile page 1
claims.uncertainty: Replacement of wording is not dissolution of the CPSU or proof that every political organization was registered.

claims.text: The first President is elected by the USSR Congress for five years and enters office upon taking the oath; this differs from the new general popular-election rule.
claims.locator: Section III.1-2; Article 127.1; facsimile pages 3 and 14
claims.uncertainty: A statutory selection rule, not evidence of who was elected or when an oath was taken.

claims.text: The dated signature block identifies M. Gorbachev as Chairman of the USSR Supreme Soviet.
claims.locator: Signature and date block; facsimile page 14
claims.uncertainty: One signed office observation; neither a complete chairmanship nor a presidential appointment.

claims.text: Section IV makes the law effective upon adoption. The instrument is dated 14 March 1990 and numbered 1360-I.
claims.locator: Section IV and instrument number/date; facsimile page 14
claims.uncertainty: No later constitutional version or office lifespan is certified by this enactment.

sources.scope_note: Claims use the reproduced primary Russian law, not the separate 2011/2024 scholarly introduction or its political interpretations. The repository cites GARF F. R-9654, Op. 1, D. 121, leaves 22-35 and the 1990 third extraordinary Congress stenographic report, volume 3, pages 192-207. Only facsimile pages 1, 3, 13 and 14 were visually reviewed. The 14 March law date must not become Gorbachev's presidential oath date.

sources.title: Diplomatic Bluebook 1990, Section 4: Soviet Union
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Japan
sources.access_method: Official HTML text read through web retrieval; separate direct HTTP download returned 403 and was not accepted as source bytes

claims.text: Japan's 1990 diplomatic account reports Gorbachev's election as General Secretary at the July 1990 CPSU congress while separately calling him President.
claims.locator: 1. Internal Politics, (1) Progress in Political Reform, July congress paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: Month-level contemporaneous diplomatic observation; original CPSU election protocol and exact election day were not inspected.

claims.text: The account reports a new Deputy General Secretary office supporting the General Secretary and supervising the Secretariat, with Vladimir Ivashkov elected.
claims.locator: 1. Internal Politics, (1) Progress in Political Reform, last paragraph
claims.uncertainty: The source spells the name Ivashkov; reconciliation with original-language identity and election records is pending. This is not a succession entitlement or a continuous deputy term.

sources.scope_note: A primary record of Japan's contemporary diplomatic reporting, not an original Soviet party register or election instrument. Retain its month precision and the reported Ivashkov spelling. No independent use is made of its shorthand for constitutional powers, its labels for new groups, or its republic-level office descriptions. The edition year is not a known website publication day.

sources.title: UN General Assembly document A/46/771 (13 December 1991): letter of 12 December 1991 from Belarus transmitting the Minsk Declaration and the Agreement establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States of 8 December 1991
sources.publisher: United Nations, General Assembly (circulated at the request of Belarus; English translation of a Russian original)

claims.text: Annex I: the leaders of the Republic of Belarus, the RSFSR and Ukraine proclaim the establishment of the Commonwealth of Independent States; signed S. Shushkevich (Chairman of the Supreme Soviet of the Republic of Belarus), B. Yeltsin (President of the RSFSR) and L. Kravchuk (President of Ukraine), Minsk, 8 December 1991.
claims.locator: PDF page 2, Annex I and signature block
claims.uncertainty: A political declaration in UN English translation. The office titles are signature observations only and are not used as holder observations.

claims.text: Annex II, preamble: the Republic of Belarus, the Russian Federation (RSFSR) and Ukraine, as founder states of the USSR and signatories of the Union Treaty of 1922, declare that the USSR as a subject of international law and a geopolitical reality no longer exists; Article 1 establishes the Commonwealth of Independent States.
claims.locator: PDF page 3, preamble and Article 1
claims.uncertainty: A statement by three republics, not an act of a USSR organ, and it does not end the USSR Presidency. The English 'no longer exists' renders the Russian present tense 'прекращает свое существование' ('ceases its existence'), shown by the GARF copy (su_garf_belovezha_copy_19911208). Signature is not entry into force.

claims.text: Article 11: from the moment of signature, the laws of third states, including the former USSR, may not be applied in the signatories' territories. Article 14: Minsk is the official seat of the coordinating bodies, and the activity of bodies of the former USSR in the territories of member states ceases. Done at Minsk, 8 December 1991; signed for the RSFSR by B. Yeltsin and G. Burbulis.
claims.locator: PDF page 6, Articles 11-14 and signature block
claims.uncertainty: Signature date only. Under the Alma-Ata Protocol of 21 December the Agreement enters into force for each party on ratification. The RSFSR ratified it on 12 December 1991 (su_rsfsr_minsk_ratification_19911212); point 2 of that ratification qualifies Article 11 by applying former-USSR norms in the RSFSR, until RSFSR legislation is adopted, insofar as they do not contradict the RSFSR Constitution, RSFSR legislation and the Agreement. The Belarus and Ukraine ratifications were not reviewed.

sources.scope_note: UN English translation of a Russian original, circulated on 13 December 1991 at the request of Belarus under a covering letter dated 12 December 1991 from its Permanent Representative. Circulation and transmission are neither signature nor ratification. Scanned PDF with an OCR layer.

claims.locator: Exhibit caption; facsimile leaves 1 and 5

sources.title: Resolution of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet No. 2014-I of 12 December 1991 'On ratification of the Agreement on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States' (original edition)
sources.publisher: Official Internet Portal of Legal Information (pravo.gov.ru), IPS 'Zakonodatelstvo Rossii' of the State System of Legal Information; the portal card cites Vedomosti S'ezda narodnykh deputatov RSFSR i Verkhovnogo Soveta RSFSR 1991 No. 51, art. 1798

claims.text: Citing point 15 of Article 109 of the RSFSR Constitution, the RSFSR Supreme Soviet ratifies the Agreement between the Republic of Belarus, the Russian Federation (RSFSR) and Ukraine on the creation of the Commonwealth of Independent States, signed at Minsk on 8 December 1991 (point 1). To give effect to Article 11 of the Agreement, it provides that until the corresponding RSFSR laws are adopted, norms of the former USSR apply in the RSFSR insofar as they do not contradict the RSFSR Constitution, RSFSR legislation and the Agreement (point 2). Signed R. I. Khasbulatov, Chairman of the RSFSR Supreme Soviet, Moscow, House of Soviets of the RSFSR, 12 December 1991, No. 2014-I.
claims.locator: Preamble, points 1-3; signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: Ratification by one party, the RSFSR, on 12 December, separate from the 8 December signature. The resolution gives no entry-into-force date of its own and no date of deposit or notification; the Alma-Ata Protocol's rule that the Agreement enters into force for each party on ratification was signed later, on 21 December. The Belarus and Ukraine ratifications were not reviewed. An act of an RSFSR body, not of a USSR organ.

sources.scope_note: RSFSR ratification of the Minsk Agreement, filed in this packet because it dates the Agreement's effect for one party and qualifies Article 11. Gazette citation: Vedomosti 1991 No. 51, art. 1798. The portal text prints the republic's name without 'Soviet' in its preamble ('Российской Федеративной Социалистической Республики'); the signed original reads the full name.

sources.title: UN document A/47/60-S/23329 (30 December 1991): letter of 27 December 1991 from Belarus transmitting the Alma-Ata Protocol, Declaration and related decisions of 21 December 1991
sources.publisher: United Nations, General Assembly and Security Council (circulated at the request of Belarus; English translation of Russian originals; the Russian-language issue of the same symbol was also read)

claims.text: Annex I, the Protocol to the Minsk Agreement: the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Republic of Armenia, the Republic of Belarus, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Republic of Kyrgyzstan, the Republic of Moldova, the Russian Federation (RSFSR), the Republic of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, the Republic of Uzbekistan and Ukraine constitute the Commonwealth of Independent States as High Contracting Parties. The Agreement establishing the Commonwealth enters into force for each party from the moment of its ratification, and documents regulating cooperation are to be drawn up taking into account the reservations made on ratification. Signed for the Russian Federation (RSFSR) by B. Yeltsin, Alma-Ata, 21 December 1991.
claims.locator: English PDF page 3, Annex I
claims.uncertainty: Georgia is not a signatory. The ratification rule is dated 21 December, after the RSFSR's ratification of 12 December. The other parties' ratification dates were not reviewed.

claims.text: Annex II, the Alma-Ata Declaration: the Commonwealth is neither a state nor a supra-state entity. The UN English text reads 'With the establishment of the Commonwealth of Independent States, the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics ceased to exist'; the Russian-language issue reads 'С образованием Содружества Независимых Государств Союз Советских Социалистических Республик прекращает свое существование' (present tense). The participants guarantee the discharge of the former USSR's treaty obligations. Signed by the same eleven leaders, Yeltsin as 'Президент Российской Федерации (РСФСР)', Alma-Ata, 21 December 1991.
claims.locator: English PDF pages 4-5, Annex II; Russian-language issue, PDF page 5
claims.uncertainty: A multilateral declaration, not an act of a USSR organ. The English past tense is not used to date the end of the USSR or of any USSR office; the Russian text is in the present tense. No text addresses the USSR Presidency or Gorbachev.

claims.text: Annex IV: a Council of Heads of State is established as the supreme organ of the Commonwealth, together with a Council of Heads of Government; plenipotentiaries are to submit by 30 December 1991 proposals on abolishing the structures of the former USSR and on the Commonwealth's coordinating bodies.
claims.locator: English PDF page 7, Annex IV
claims.uncertainty: An instruction to propose abolition, not the abolition of any named USSR office.

sources.scope_note: UN English translation of Russian originals, circulated on 30 December 1991 under a covering letter dated 27 December 1991 from the Permanent Representative of Belarus; transmission is not signature. The English PDF is an OCR-reconstructed rendering with visible recognition errors. Annex III (interim command of the armed forces assigned to Marshal E. I. Shaposhnikov) and Annex V (support for Russia's continuance of the USSR's membership of the UN and other international organizations) were verified but are not imported: they concern no institution in this packet, and continuity of UN membership is not a domestic institutional mapping.

sources.title: Memorandum of telephone conversation: telcon with Mikhail Gorbachev, President of the Soviet Union, 25 December 1991, 10:03-10:25 a.m., Camp David
sources.publisher: US National Archives (NARA) catalog copy; George H. W. Bush Presidential Records, National Security Council, Presidential Telcon Files, OA/ID CF01730, folder CF01730-013

claims.text: The White House memorandum identifies the other party to a call on 25 December 1991, 10:03-10:25 a.m., at Camp David, as 'Mikhail Gorbachev, President of the Soviet Union'; interpreter Dmitri Zarechnak, notetaker Nicholas Burns of the NSC staff.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, subject, participants and date lines
claims.uncertainty: A US record; the times are the US side's and no time zone is printed. An office observation, not a term.

claims.text: Gorbachev says he had considered making his statement on Tuesday or that day and decided to make it that day, at the end of the day; in about two hours he will speak on Moscow TV with a short statement about his decision.
claims.locator: PDF page 1, second and third Gorbachev paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: A stated intention before the broadcast, in a translated memorandum rather than a verbatim transcript.

claims.text: Gorbachev says he has on his desk a decree of the President of the USSR on his resignation; he will also resign his duties as Commander-in-Chief and transfer authority to use nuclear weapons to the President of the Russian Federation, and as soon as he announces his resignation he will put these decrees into effect. Bush later notes that the constitutional responsibilities on this issue have been passed to Boris Yeltsin.
claims.locator: PDF page 2, paragraph beginning 'Now, about Russia'; PDF page 3, first paragraph
claims.uncertainty: A report of intent, not the instruments. Whether a decree on resignation existed separately from decree UP-3162 is not established. The transfer of nuclear-use authority to the President of the Russian Federation is not an institutional succession from the USSR Presidency.

sources.scope_note: Declassified on 23 September 2008 (stamp: E.O. 12958 as amended, 2004-1975-MR). Scanned PDF; page 4 is the library's citation sheet, not a textual record. The bush41library.tamu.edu copy redirected to a homepage and was not used.

sources.publisher: George H.W. Bush Presidential Library and Museum (NARA), Public Papers of the Presidents

claims.text: Speaking at 9 p.m. from the Oval Office, Bush says that the formation of the Commonwealth of Independent States 'marks the end of the old Soviet Union, signified today by Mikhail Gorbachev's decision to resign as President', and that he spoke with Gorbachev that morning.
claims.locator: Paragraphs 5-6 and closing note
claims.uncertainty: A foreign head of state's characterization after the event: it reports a decision to resign that day, not an instrument or an effective moment.

claims.text: USSR Law No. 1861-I of 26 December 1990, adopted by the Congress of People's Deputies, renames Chapter 16 of the Constitution 'Кабінет Міністрів СРСР' (item 19) and rewrites Articles 128-136 (items 20-28): new Article 128 makes the Cabinet of Ministers the executive and administrative body of the USSR, subordinate to the President; new Article 129 composes it of the Prime Minister ('Прем'єр-міністр'), his deputies and USSR ministers, its structure set by the Supreme Soviet on the President's proposal; Article 134 is deleted; new Article 136 leaves the Cabinet's competence and procedure to a USSR law. Items 2, 4, 10, 11 and 29 substitute the Cabinet of Ministers for the 'Government of the USSR' in Article 77 and for the Council of Ministers in Articles 96, 122, 124 and 140. Signed 'Президент Союзу Радянських Соціалістичних Республік М.ГОРБАЧОВ', Moscow, Kremlin, 26 December 1990, No. 1861-I.
claims.locator: Items 2, 4, 10, 11, 19-21, 26, 28 and 29; signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only; it dates no holder's start or end. The law renames the chapter and rewrites its articles; it does not say it creates the Cabinet, and it has no entry-into-force clause of its own (Law 1862-I of the same day puts it into force on adoption, su_law_1862i_council_of_ministers_retains_powers_19901226). When the Council of Ministers ceased and the Cabinet was formed is not stated. A Ukrainian-language database text, not the Russian original.

ЛУКЬЯНОВ' (initial and surname only).
claims.locator: Art. 1000, printed p. 1420 (PDF p. 14); signature and date block
claims.uncertainty: An in-office signature before the holder observation of 22 August: a role claim only, not a start or an end.

claims.text: Presidium resolution No. 2352-I 'О неотложных мерах по восстановлению конституционного порядка в стране' (art. 1001), 'Москва, Кремль 21 августа 1991 г.', declares illegal the de facto removal of President 'М. С. Горбачева' from his constitutional duties and demands that Vice-President 'Г. И. Янаева' revoke his decrees; it is signed 'Председатель Верховного Совета СССР А. ЛУКЬЯНОВ'.
claims.locator: Art. 1001, printed p. 1420 (PDF p. 14)
claims.uncertainty: An in-office signature: a role claim only. The gazette's own report (su_ved35_presidium_under_chamber_chairs_19910821) says the Presidium sitting of 21-22 August was led by the chamber chairmen; the two records are not reconciled here.

claims.text: Presidium resolutions No. 2353-I (art. 1002: consent to the prosecution and arrest of USSR people's deputies 'Бакланова О. Д., Стародубцева В. А., Болдина В. И., Варенникова В. И. и Шенина О. С.') and No. 2354-I (art. 1003: the proposed agenda of the extraordinary session), both 'Москва, Кремль. 22 августа 1991 г.', are each signed 'Председатель Верховного Совета СССР А. ЛУКЬЯНОВ' (initial and surname only).
claims.locator: Arts. 1002-1003, printed p. 1421 (PDF p. 15)
claims.uncertainty: The latest in-office signatures of his reviewed: an attestation on the acts' date, not an end. The same day's Presidium resolution removing him from conducting sittings is known only by reference (su_ss_res_2361i_presidium_removal_reference_19910822), so the order of these acts within 22 August is unknown.

claims.text: Resolution 2354-I proposes, as item 5 of the extraordinary session's agenda, 'Об изменениях в составе Правительства СССР и других государственных органов'.
claims.locator: Art. 1003, item 5, printed p. 1421 (PDF p. 15)
claims.uncertainty: A proposed agenda item about the Government's composition, found by the independent check of part B; it decides nothing and names no one.

claims.text: Decree of the President of the USSR 'Об освобождении Павлова В. С. от обязанностей Премьер-министра СССР' (art. 1008), 'Москва, Кремль. 22 августа 1991 г. № УП-2443', signed 'Президент Союза Советских Социалистических Республик М. ГОРБАЧЕВ', resolves to 'освободить Павлова Валентина Сергеевича от обязанностей Премьер-министра СССР'.
claims.locator: Art. 1008, printed p. 1423 (PDF p. 17)
claims.uncertainty: A presidential release decree without an effect clause that refers the decision to the Supreme Soviet (su_ukaz_up2443_referred_to_vs_session_19910822), whose agreement came on 28 August (su_vs_2366i_agrees_to_pavlov_release_19910828). Neither act states the day the office ended, so no until is set; an integrator ruling is requested.

claims.text: Decree УП-2443 gives as its ground 'возбуждением Прокуратурой Союза ССР уголовного дела в отношении Павлова В. С. за участие в антиконституционном заговоре'.
claims.locator: Art. 1008, opening clause, printed p. 1423 (PDF p. 17)
claims.uncertainty: Reports that proceedings exist; it gives no date for opening the case and says nothing of an arrest, which remains unsourced.

claims.text: Decree УП-2443 directs: 'Внести данное решение на рассмотрение сессии Верховного Совета СССР.'
claims.locator: Art. 1008, second paragraph, printed p. 1423 (PDF p. 17)
claims.uncertainty: Consistent with Article 127-3(6) (release by agreement with the Supreme Soviet); the agreement is resolution 2366-I of 28 August.

claims.text: Decree 'Об отмене антиконституционных актов организаторов государственного переворота' (art. 1009), 'Москва, Кремль. 22 августа 1991 г. № УП-2444': annuls all decisions issued by the ГКЧП or its individual members (point 1), 'Отстранить всех членов ГКЧП от занимаемых постов' (point 2), and notes that the Prosecutor General of the USSR has opened a criminal case against the participants in the conspiracy (point 3).
claims.locator: Art. 1009, points 1-3 and signature block, printed pp. 1423-1424 (PDF pp. 17-18)
claims.uncertainty: Names nobody; the Premier is listed among the ГКЧП members only later, in resolution 2371-I of 29 August. Not used as an end; kept distinct from УП-2443.

claims.text: Decree 'О Кабинете Министров СССР' (art. 1025), 'Москва, Кремль 24 августа 1991 г. № УП-2461', point 1: because the Cabinet 'не выполнил своего конституционного долга и не принял необходимых мер для срыва государственного заговора, а отдельные члены Кабинета прямо в нем участвовали', under Article 14 of the USSR Law 'О Кабинете Министров СССР' the President puts before the Supreme Soviet 'вопрос о доверии Кабинету Министров СССР'.
claims.locator: Art. 1025, point 1, printed p. 1429 (PDF p. 23)
claims.uncertainty: Raises the question only; the no-confidence resolution is 2367-I of 28 August.

claims.text: Point 2: 'Для организации совместно с республиками оперативного управления народным хозяйством страны создать Комитет во главе с Силаевым И. С. (руководитель), Вольским А. И., Лужковым Ю. М., Явлинским Г. А. (заместители)', who are to determine its membership and within two days appoint those responsible for particular areas.
claims.locator: Art. 1025, point 2 and signature block, printed p. 1429 (PDF p. 23)
claims.uncertainty: Creates an unnamed committee while the Cabinet had not been dismissed; it does not call the committee the Government or its 'руководитель' head of the Union government. A claim on the institution only: never a holder of su_government_head and not acting service in that role.

claims.text: The gazette's report 'Заседание Президиума Верховного Совета СССР' states that on 21-22 August the Presidium met in the Kremlin 'под руководством председателей палат Верховного Совета СССР И. Д. Лаптева и Р. Н. Нишанова', consented to the prosecution and arrest of five deputies, proposed the session's agenda and, on a proposal of a group of deputies, entrusted the chairing of the extraordinary session alternately to the chamber chairmen.
claims.locator: Section Three ('Раздел третий'), printed p. 1431 (PDF p. 25)
claims.uncertainty: An official gazette report, not an act, covering a sitting of 21-22 August without a single day. Chamber chairmen presiding is not acting service as Chairman of the Supreme Soviet; claim only. It sits uneasily with the Presidium acts of 21 and 22 August printed with his signature (su_lukyanov_signs_presidium_2352i_19910821, su_lukyanov_signs_presidium_2353i_2354i_19910822); the sequence within those days is not stated. The same section's sentence on the 26 August suspension is not imported (resolution 2361-I carries it).

claims.text: Supreme Soviet resolution 'О недоверии Кабинету Министров СССР' (art. 1033), 'Москва, Кремль 28 августа 1991 г. № 2367-I': having considered the President's decree of 24 August 1991 'О Кабинете Министров СССР', under Article 130 of the Constitution the Supreme Soviet resolves '1. claims.text: Point 2: 'Впредь до образования нового состава Кабинета Министров СССР для организации совместно с республиками оперативного управления народным хозяйством страны создать Комитет по оперативному управлению народным хозяйством СССР во главе с тов. Силаевым И. С.'
claims.locator: Art. 1033, point 2, printed p. 1443 (PDF p. 13)
claims.uncertainty: An interim body created until a new Cabinet is formed; the resolution does not call the Committee the Government or its head the head of the Union government. A claim on the institution only: never a holder and not acting service in su_government_head.

claims.text: Supreme Soviet resolution 'О даче согласия на привлечение к уголовной ответственности и арест народного депутата СССР Лукьянова А. И.' (art. 1034), 'Москва, Кремль. 29 августа 1991 г. № 2368-I': under Article 34 of the USSR Law on the status of a people's deputy, consent is given to 'привлечение к уголовной ответственности и арест народного депутата СССР Лукьянова Анатолия Ивановича'.
claims.locator: Art. 1034, printed p. 1443 (PDF p. 13)
claims.uncertainty: Consent only; the arrest itself and its date are not stated by any reviewed primary source. The act styles him a people's deputy, not Chairman; it is not an end of office.

claims.text: Supreme Soviet resolution 'О ситуации, возникшей в стране в связи с имевшим место государственным переворотом' (art. 1038, 29 August 1991, No. 2371-I) states that the coup of the night of 18-19 August 1991 was organised by members of the unconstitutionally formed ГКЧП, listing among them 'Премьер-министр СССР Павлов В. С.'.
claims.locator: Art. 1038, first paragraph, printed p. 1445 (PDF p. 15); signature block, printed p. 1447 (PDF p. 17)
claims.uncertainty: A retrospective description of 18-19 August, adopted after the 28 August agreement; not an attestation that he held office on 29 August and not a boundary.

claims.text: The gazette's report 'Сессия Верховного Совета СССР', in the paragraph beginning '28 августа', states that during the discussion of the role of the Supreme Soviet's leadership in the events from 18 August 'Председатель Верховного Совета СССР А. И. Лукьянов дал объяснение по поводу своих действий в этот период'.
claims.locator: Section Three ('Раздел третий'), paragraph beginning '28 августа', printed pp. 1468-1469 (PDF pp. 38-39)
claims.uncertainty: The date comes from the paragraph's '28 августа' opening. The same section's report of the 29 August consent is not imported (resolution 2368-I carries it).

claims.text: The same paragraph reports that at the agenda item on confidence in the Cabinet, after the first deputy Premiers 'В. И Щербаков и В. X. Догужиев' addressed the sitting, 'Верховный Совет согласился с Указом Президента СССР об освобождении В. С. Павлова от обязанностей Премьер-министра СССР'.
claims.locator: Section Three, paragraph beginning '28 августа', printed p. 1469 (PDF p. 39)
claims.uncertainty: The date comes from the paragraph's '28 августа' opening; no vote figures are printed. The first deputy Premiers' appearance is not an acting designation. Split from the no-confidence report at the independent check's request.

claims.locator: Section Three, paragraph beginning '28 августа', printed p. 1469 (PDF p. 39)
claims.uncertainty: The date comes from the paragraph's '28 августа' opening; no vote figures are printed. An act about the Cabinet as a body.

claims.text: The report states that on 31 August 'Председатель Совета Союза И. Д. Лаптев в своем выступлении подвел итоги работы сессии', after which the extraordinary session ended.
claims.locator: Section Three, printed p. 1470 (PDF p. 40)
claims.uncertainty: A chamber chairman summing up the session; not acting service as Chairman of the Supreme Soviet. Claim only, never a holder.

claims.text: Resolution of the Congress of People's Deputies of the USSR 'Об освобождении А. И. Лукьянова от обязанностей Председателя Верховного Совета СССР' (art. 1079), 'Москва, Кремль, 4 сентября 1991 г. № 2389-I', signed 'СЪЕЗД НАРОДНЫХ ДЕПУТАТОВ СССР': 'Освободить Лукьянова Анатолия Ивановича от обязанностей Председателя Верховного Совета СССР.'
claims.locator: Art. 1079, printed p. 1485 (PDF p. 15)
claims.uncertainty: The act is dated 4 September but states no entry-into-force rule or effective moment. Under the rule applied to every holder in this packet (and in CLAUDE-C01-19), a release without a stated effective day is a dated release claim and sets no until; an integrator ruling is requested. An act of the Congress, not of the Supreme Soviet.

claims.text: USSR Law No. 2392-I 'Об органах государственной власти и управления Союза ССР в переходный период' (art. 1082), 'Москва, Кремль. 5 сентября 1991 г.', signed 'Президент Союза Советских Социалистических Республик М. ГОРБАЧЕВ': Articles 1-2 make the Supreme Soviet, in the transitional period, the highest representative body, consisting of two independent chambers, the Council of Republics (20 deputies per union republic delegated by the republics' highest bodies, 52 for the RSFSR, one vote per union republic) and the Council of the Union (formed by republic deputations of USSR people's deputies), and divide their competences.
claims.locator: Art. 1082, Articles 1-2, printed p. 1487 (PDF p. 17)
claims.uncertainty: Statute text: procedure only, never a date for any office. The law provides no office of Chairman of the Supreme Soviet; it mentions only the chairmen of the chambers (Article 7).

claims.text: Law 2392-I, Articles 4-5: the post of Vice-President is abolished (Article 4); to coordinate the management of the national economy and concerted economic reform and social policy, the union republics form on a parity basis an Inter-republican Economic Committee, whose Chairman 'назначается Президентом СССР с согласия Государственного Совета СССР'; the Committee and the heads of all-union bodies are accountable to the President, the State Council and the Supreme Soviet (Article 5).
claims.locator: Art. 1082, Articles 4-5, printed pp. 1487-1488 (PDF pp. 17-18)
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. The law does not call the Committee the Government or its Chairman head of the Union government.

claims.text: Law 2392-I, Articles 7 and 9: the President convenes the first sitting of the new Supreme Soviet no later than 2 October 1991; until the new Supreme Soviet begins work 'сохраняются полномочия существующего Верховного Совета СССР, сессия которого может быть созвана председателями палат'; the law enters into force on publication, except Article 2, which takes effect from the opening of the first session of the new Supreme Soviet.
claims.locator: Art. 1082, Articles 7 and 9 and signature block, printed p. 1488 (PDF p. 18)
claims.uncertainty: Procedure only. The publication day that brought the law into force is not verified here (this gazette issue is dated 11 September).

claims.text: Decree of the President of the USSR 'О статусе Комитета по оперативному управлению народным хозяйством СССР' (art. 1090), 'Москва, Кремль. 6 сентября 1991 г. № УП-2528': 'Учитывая необходимость обеспечения преемственности структур исполнительной власти', the Committee, until the Inter-republican Economic Committee is formed, performs the functions of current management of the country's economic and social life 'возлагавшиеся ранее на Кабинет Министров СССР' (point 1), and exercises the rights and bears the obligations arising from international treaties and agreements previously concluded by the Government of the USSR (point 2).
claims.locator: Art. 1090, printed p. 1496 (PDF p. 26)
claims.uncertainty: Assigns the former Cabinet's current-management functions to the Committee as an interim body ('впредь до сформирования'); it names no person and does not call the Committee's head the head of the Union government. Interim arrangement: claims only.

claims.text: The gazette's report 'Съезд народных депутатов СССР' states that on 4 September 'Постановлениями Съезда освобождены от обязанностей Председателя Верховного Совета СССР А. И. Лукьянов и Вице-президента СССР Г. И. Янаев'.
claims.locator: Section Three ('Раздел третий'), printed p. 1501 (PDF p. 31)

Each holder observation rests on an in-office signature or on the Supreme Soviet's approval and carries attested_on only: no reviewed source states the day any holder assumed office or the day any holder's office ended, so no holder has from or until, and no end is taken from a successor's approval, a release decree, the Supreme Soviet's agreement with it, a no-confidence resolution, illness or a retrospective styling. Observations are recorded at the earliest and latest reviewed attestation of each person in the period; intermediate and pre-period signatures are role claims. Acting and interim service (the report for the government of 27 December 1990, a Deputy Chairman's signature of 10 January 1991, order 943р of 19 August 1991) are claims only, never holders or boundaries.
